assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks made an exceptional advance in control of quantum matter and precision measurement, with fundamental and practical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept, while Ye made decisive experimental realizations and advances.
assessment.maturity: The clocks are repeatedly demonstrated at extraordinary accuracy and have become a robust international platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made quantum optics with engineered superconducting atoms experimentally controllable and opened a powerful new regime of quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Girvin supplied seminal theoretical architecture, and Schoelkopf led foundational experimental realization; the proposed trio is coherent.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena and methods have been reproduced broadly and are central to contemporary superconducting quantum science.
uncertainties: The field overlaps conceptually with recently recognized superconducting-circuit advances, requiring careful delineation of the distinct discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric and topological phases changed the physical understanding of quantum mechanics and have consequences across condensed matter and quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Berry and Aharonov are the clear names attached to complementary foundational phase effects.
assessment.maturity: The effects are experimentally established and conceptually indispensable after decades of use.
uncertainties: The relation between the Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase may make a single prize formulation historically and conceptually broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their proposals gave quantum computation and simulation a compelling physical route using controllable atomic systems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller form an unusually clear partnership for foundational architectures and protocols.
assessment.maturity: Trapped-ion and neutral-atom platforms now realize key elements of their vision across laboratories.
uncertainties: The wider development involved many experimental and theoretical contributors, so the precise prize boundary needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light converted a quantum-optical resource into a demonstrated means of surpassing conventional measurement limits.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the decisive quantum-metrological framework, while Schnabel made major experimental advances toward precision application.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is a reproducible laboratory capability and is deployed in gravitational-wave observatories.
uncertainties: Attribution across the development of squeezed-state generation, theory, and interferometric implementation is broader than this pair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall and topological-insulator programme revealed a new class of electronic quantum matter with protected boundary phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal, and Molenkamp led a landmark experimental observation.
assessment.maturity: The central effects are extensively reproduced and have reshaped condensed-matter research.
uncertainties: The experimental and theoretical topological-insulator landscape has several plausible prize formulations and contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics enabled radiation-pressure control and quantum measurement of mechanical motion, uniting photonics with macroscopic motion.
assessment.attribution: The proposed researchers made foundational and complementary contributions to high-quality optomechanical systems and their quantum control.
assessment.maturity: The field has mature experimental benchmarks, including cooling and measurement close to the quantum regime.
uncertainties: Credit for the field's formative theoretical concepts and early experiments is distributed across a broad community.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade transformed neutral atoms into a controllable many-body and programmable quantum platform.
assessment.attribution: Saffman established key blockade and gate concepts, while Browaeys and Lukin led decisive programmable-array experiments.
assessment.maturity: Large arrays and programmable interactions have been reproduced in several laboratories and already enable new quantum simulations.
uncertainties: The platform remains rapidly evolving, and its ultimate scientific and technological scope is not yet settled.
